text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, I can hear you. Bit of a delay maybe.
A: That's my wifi, honestly, it's been rubbish all week. I'm Hodan, I'm in Wembley.
B: Kerry. Bridgwater. Somerset.
A: Oh nice, I've never been. Did you do that puzzle thing at the start? Because I'm not gonna lie, I think I smashed it, I finished with like a minute left.
B: Good for you. I just sort of guessed the last couple, to be honest. I was starving.
A: Ha! Fair. So what do you do? I had you down as, erm, I don't know, you look like you've had a long day.
B: Cheers.
A: No, I mean that nicely, I've had a long day as well!
B: Yeah, I'm a painter and decorator. Self-employed. I've been on a stairwell all day, so yeah, you was right, I'm knackered.
A: Oh, that's proper hard work, though. On your feet all day.
B: It's the ladders that get you. And the back. What about you, are you a nurse? I thought nurse with the lanyard.
A: Everyone thinks that. No, I'm a senior pharmacy technician, so I'm in the aseptic unit and the dispensary, I do all the final accuracy checking and I run the checking rota. Basically if something's wrong it doesn't leave the department, because I've caught it. I actually keep my own spreadsheet of near-misses, which my manager loves, by the way, she uses it in all her meetings now.
B: Right. So you're the one who tells everyone off.
A: Kind of, yeah! Somebody's got to.
B: No, I get it. I'm the same with prep. If someone's not filled a wall properly I can see it from the doorway, and then I'm the one who looks bad when the paint goes on.
A: Exactly, it comes back on you, you know. Do you work on your own, then?
B: Yeah, just me. Domestic mostly, and some stuff for a lettings agent. Word of mouth, Facebook groups. Busy now, but January's always dead.
A: Is that the boy in your kitchen? No, sorry, that's my wall, I'm thinking of mine. I've got a son, Idris, he's eight. The photo behind me.
B: Oh right, yeah, I saw that. Red jumper. I've got one, Jayden, he's fourteen.
A: Fourteen! Is he a nightmare?
B: He's alright. He's at that age, you know. Grunts at me. Plays football Sundays, so I'm stood on a touchline every week in the rain.
A: Oh my days, don't talk to me about football. Idris has just joined a club and the kit alone, like, sixty quid, for shorts and a top he's gonna grow out of by Christmas. I'm gonna flog it on Vinted after, obviously.
B: I'm always on Vinted. That's how I get all my bags.
A: Yes! See, people think it's tight but it's just sense, isn't it?
B: It's just sense. Do you do it all on your own, then? With your boy?
A: Yeah, it's just me and him. My mum helps loads, she does pickups when I'm on lates, I'd be stuck without her, honestly. His dad's in Leicester, so he just turns up in the holidays and gets to be the fun one, you know.
B: Ha. Yeah. Mine's in Taunton. Every other weekend, takes him to Nando's, he's a hero.
A: Every time! Every single time, it's Nando's. Sorry, go on.
B: No, that's it really. You just get on with it, don't you? Nobody else is going to.
A: Nobody. And then people want to give you their opinion on top, like my aunties, oh my God, the aunties—
